request: Wie viel gebe ich im Schnitt pro Woche aus, Monat fuer Monat?

plan.title: Ausgaben pro Woche im Monatsverlauf
plan.question: Ausgaben 2025 je Monat, umgerechnet auf eine Woche (Monatssumme mal sieben geteilt durch die Tage des Monats), eine Zeile pro Monat, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM' und per_week_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) * 7.0 / CAST(strftime('%d', date(booked_on, 'start of month', '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS INTEGER), 2) AS per_week_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

plan.question: Durchschnittliche Ausgabe je Buchung je Monat und Konto 2025, die Summe des Monats auf dem Konto geteilt durch die Zahl seiner Buchungen, eine Zeile je Monat und Konto, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM', account und avg_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       account,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY month, account
ORDER BY month, account
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
zwei Konten werden ueber die Monate verglichen, also zwei Serien
eine Linie je Konto liest sich direkter als vierundzwanzig Balken
das Konto ist die Serie, der Monat die Position
die Spalten sind month, account und avg_eur, die Euro-Spalte zuletzt
reasoning_code:
the shape is line and these rows carry a series, so one lineY over all of them
the columns are month, account and avg_eur, and avg_eur holds the numbers
account names the series, so it is the z and the color channel and the legend goes on
months on x with monthShort, the euro domain over every figure in the rows, zero included

request: What was the biggest single booking on the joint account in each month?

plan.title: Largest booking on the joint account
plan.question: The largest single spending booking on the account Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto for each month of 2025, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and largest_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       ROUND(MAX(-amount), 2) AS largest_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND account = 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
it names one of the two accounts, so the other one is filtered out
it asks for one single booking per month, never a total
the columns are month and largest_eur
the period is the whole year 2025, one bar per month
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar, so the mark is barY over the rows
the columns are month and largest_eur, and largest_eur holds the numbers
months on x on a band scale with monthShort, euros on y
a bar rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory

request: Als Ring: wie verteilt sich das Geld auf meinem Privatkonto auf die Kategorien, in denen ich am oeftesten buche?

plan.title: Anteile auf dem Privatkonto
plan.question: Ausgaben 2025 auf dem Konto Sparkasse Stuttgart Privatkonto Jonas je Kategorie, nur die sechs Kategorien mit den meisten Buchungen auf diesem Konto, unkategorisierte als 'Needs review', absteigend nach Betrag, Spalten topic und total_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND account = 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Privatkonto Jonas'
  AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (
    SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review')
    FROM transaction_view
    WHERE amount < 0 AND account = 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Privatkonto Jonas'
    GROUP BY coalesce(category, 'Needs review')
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
    LIMIT 6
  )
GROUP BY topic
ORDER BY total_eur DESC
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
sie nennt ein Konto von zweien, das andere faellt also weg
sie fragt nach Anteilen, und die Haeufigkeit waehlt die sechs Stuecke aus
die Spalten sind topic und total_eur
der Zeitraum ist das Jahr 2025
reasoning_code:
the shape is doughnut, so pie allocates the slices and radialArc draws them
the columns are topic and total_eur, and total_eur is the value pie reads
topic names each slice, so it is the color channel and the key, and the legend goes on
a doughnut has no axes, so scales.x and scales.y are both null

request: On the joint account, which of the shops we use at least fifteen times costs the most per visit?

plan.title: Average per visit, joint account
plan.question: Average spending per booking on the account Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto for every merchant with at least fifteen bookings there in 2025, the merchant named by its enriched title, sorted by the average, columns merchant and avg_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND account = 'Sparkasse Stuttgart Gemeinschaftskonto'
GROUP BY merchant
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 15
ORDER BY avg_eur DESC
LIMIT 10
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
it names one of the two accounts, so the other one is filtered out
it ranks shops by what one visit costs, and the count decides who is ranked
long shop names read along the axis of a horizontal bar
the columns are merchant and avg_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_horizontal, so the mark is barX and nothing else
the columns are merchant and avg_eur, and avg_eur holds the numbers
barX draws sideways, so the euros are x and the shop names are y
scales.x is the euro axis with the grid, scales.y the band of names, none dropped

request: Wie summieren sich die Ausgaben der beiden Konten ueber das Jahr auf, nebeneinander?

plan.title: Aufsummiert, Konto gegen Konto
plan.question: Laufende Summe der Ausgaben 2025 innerhalb jedes Kontos, eine Zeile je Monat und Konto, die laufende Summe je Konto, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM', account und cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, account, SUM(-amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY month, account
)
SELECT month, account,
       ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (PARTITION BY account ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM months
ORDER BY account, month
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
"aufsummieren" ist eine laufende Summe, also eine Flaeche, und beide Konten stehen nebeneinander
das Konto ist die Serie, also ein Band je Konto und eine Legende
die Achse ist der Monat, beide Baender beginnen im Januar
die Spalten sind month, account und cumulative_eur, die Euro-Spalte zuletzt
reasoning_code:
the shape is area and these rows carry a series, so one areaY and one lineY over all of them
the columns are month, account and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
account names the series, so it is the z and the color channel on both marks and the legend goes on
the two bands are compared and not added, so each rests on zero: y1 zero, y2 the figure

request: Was geben wir pro Tag aus, Monat fuer Monat, und wie verteilt sich das auf die beiden Konten?

plan.title: Tagessatz nach Konto
plan.question: Ausgaben je Monat und Konto 2025, jeweils geteilt durch die Zahl der Tage des Monats, eine Zeile je Monat und Konto, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM', account und per_day_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       account,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) / CAST(strftime('%d', date(booked_on, 'start of month', '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS INTEGER), 2) AS per_day_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY month, account
ORDER BY month, account
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
sie fragt nach einem Tagessatz und zugleich nach seiner Aufteilung auf die Konten
gestapelte Balken tragen beides, die Hoehe und die Teile
das Konto ist die Serie, der Monat die Position
die Spalten sind month, account und per_day_eur, die Euro-Spalte zuletzt
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_stacked, so barY carries a series and no layout
the columns are month, account and per_day_eur, and per_day_eur holds the numbers
account names the series, so it is the z and the color channel and the legend goes on
the stack is taller than any single row, so the euro axis names no domain

request: Show the money running from each account into the shops we use at least twenty-five times.

plan.title: From account to frequent shop
plan.question: Spending of 2025 per account and merchant, only for merchants with at least twenty-five bookings over both accounts, one row per account and merchant, every amount positive, columns from_account, to_merchant and amount_eur.

sql:
SELECT account AS from_account,
       coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS to_merchant,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
  AND coalesce(title, counterparty, description) IN (
    SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description)
    FROM transaction_view
    WHERE amount < 0
    GROUP BY coalesce(title, counterparty, description)
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 25
  )
GROUP BY from_account, to_merchant
ORDER BY amount_eur DESC
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
it asks where the money runs, from the two accounts into the shops, which is a flow
a sankey is the shape that draws a flow
how often a shop is used chooses which shops are in the picture
the columns are from_account, to_merchant and amount_eur, every amount positive
reasoning_code:
the shape is sankey, so sankeyDiagram lays the flow out and the child marks draw it
the columns are from_account, to_merchant and amount_eur, and amount_eur holds the numbers
the node list is every name on either end of a link, each one once
there is no x and no y on a flow, so both positional scales are null
